maintainer_vibe: Process-driven volunteer moderators who enforce compliance with written policies. A GitHub Actions bot handles initial PR validation: checklist completion, conventional commit title format, dedicated branch usage, and linked issue requirements. Human maintainers intervene for substantive issues and consistently cite the FAQ or contributing guide. Tone is direct and policy-referenced rather than conversational, but they praise successful first contributions explicitly.
pr_guidelines: PR titles must follow the conventional commits format: type(scope): description, with description under 30 characters. Types are fix, feat, refactor, docs. Enforced by bot auto-renaming and maintainer correction. Actual maintainer feedback on PR #69544: 'Please follow freeCodeCamp's convention for PR title.'

The PR description checklist must be genuinely completed. A GitHub Actions bot automatically comments when items are missing or unchecked, as seen on PRs #69746 and #66124 where the bot listed all four required checklist items and refused to proceed.

PRs must target an issue labeled help wanted or first timers only, and that issue must be open for contribution. The bot checks this automatically. Maintainer plamoni closed PR #69746 with: 'The related issue has not yet been opened for contribution, so we are not accepting PRs for it.'
raw_summary: freeCodeCamp runs a high-volume repository (455k stars, 46k forks) with a volunteer-driven review process. A GitHub Actions bot enforces initial PR compliance: checklist completion, conventional commit title format, dedicated branch usage, and linked issue requirements. Human maintainers (imsomilg, plamoni, a2937, majestic-owl448, Sembauke, jdwilkin4) intervene for substantive issues and consistently cite written policies from the FAQ and contributing guide. Three key maintainer behaviors emerge from recent closed PRs: direct correction of PR title convention violations, immediate rejection of AI-generated contributions (PRs #69746 and #69748 were both closed for Claude Code attribution and unopened issues), and thorough test-coverage nitpicks on curriculum changes (PR #66235 went through 5 review rounds over 4 months). The FAQ explicitly states AI-generated comments and responses will not be engaged with. Stale PRs are closed after inactivity with a brief 'Closed due to inactivity~' comment. The repository uses a deprioritized label for low-effort submissions and directs contributors to Discord or the community forum for questions rather than pinging maintainers. Successful first-time contributors receive explicit praise: 'Congrats on your first pull request (PR)!' and 'We are happy to accept these changes and look forward to future contributions.'
maintainer_persona: Policy-enforcing volunteer moderators. They automate initial review compliance via a bot, then apply written rules directly when escalating to human review. They reject AI-generated content firmly, close stale PRs casually, and redirect questions to community channels rather than engaging in back-and-forth. On curriculum PRs they iterate extensively with detailed technical feedback until tests are comprehensive.
top_dos: Follow the conventional commit PR title format (type(scope): description under 30 chars) and include a genuinely completed PR checklist in the description
Open PRs from a dedicated feature branch targeting freeCodeCamp main, confirm local testing, and include Playwright integration tests for behavioral changes
Only submit PRs against issues labeled help wanted or first timers only; verify the issue is open for contribution before starting work
top_donts: Do not edit files directly through GitHub's web editor; all changes must come from a fork on a dedicated feature branch
Do not submit AI-generated content in PR descriptions, comments, or responses; the FAQ states maintainers will not engage with AI-generated replies
Do not @mention maintainers or reviewers; use the freeCodeCamp Community Discord channel or forum instead

deep_sections.title: What Contributors Actually Say
deep_sections.body: The contributor base is mixed between first-time participants and repeat contributors. PR #69544 by sultan-web22 included a checklist in the description but used a non-conventional title ('fix: added headers to user psuedo-class'), prompting imsomilg to write 'Please follow freeCodeCamp's convention for PR title.' PR #69746 by aqibali12 included a detailed root-cause analysis and test plan but was flagged for being generated with Claude Code. PR #69748 by Iitian001 targeted an issue not yet open for contribution and was also Claude Code generated. Contributors who follow conventions and avoid AI attributions receive praise for first PRs and smooth merges thereafter, suggesting that compliance with the checklist and title format is the primary filter for first review.

deep_sections.title: Hidden Friction Signals
deep_sections.body: Three friction points are visible in recent closed PRs: (1) The deprioritized label (seen on PR #69748) marks submissions as low-effort, reducing maintainer attention. (2) PRs targeting issues not yet open for contribution are closed immediately regardless of code quality, as plamoni noted on PR #69746: 'The related issue has not yet been opened for contribution, so we are not accepting PRs for it.' (3) AI-generated attribution in PR descriptions triggers a policy-based closure, as a2937 wrote on PR #69748, quoting the FAQ that maintainers will not engage with AI-generated content. The GitHub Actions bot's checklist and branch enforcement creates a two-layer gate: automation catches formatting issues, then human maintainers escalate policy violations. On curriculum PRs, reviewers enforce scope discipline: majestic-owl448 on PR #66235 said 'please cease working on learn-localstorage-by-buidling-a-todo-app, this is archived material that we don't update anymore'.

deep_sections.title: Unwritten Rules
deep_sections.body: Beyond the written contributing guide, three norms govern success: (1) PR titles must match the conventional commits spec with a scope, as demonstrated by the maintainer correction on PR #69544 and the bot auto-renaming PR #66124. (2) The contributing guide states 'Following the guidelines carefully earns you the respect of fellow maintainers and saves everyone time,' signaling that procedural compliance is valued over raw code quality alone. (3) Stale PRs are closed casually with 'Closed due to inactivity~' (from imsomilg on PR #69544), suggesting a 21-day inactivity threshold after a status: waiting update label is applied. Contributors should expect automated bot feedback first, with human review reserved for issues that pass the initial compliance filter.
